claim: Imaging endogenous mRNAs in live animals is technically challenging.
source: Imaging endogenous mRNAs in live animals is technically challenging.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that reflects established knowledge in the field about the difficulty of imaging endogenous mRNAs in live animals.

claim: MS2-based signal amplification with the Suntag system enables live-cell RNA imaging of high temporal resolution with 8xMS2 stem-loops.
source: Here, we describe an MS2-based signal amplification with the Suntag system that enables live-cell RNA imaging of high temporal resolution and with 8xMS2 stem-loops, which overcomes the obstacle of inserting a 1300 nt 24xMS2 into the genome for the imaging of endogenous mRNAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing successful RNA imaging using the MASS system with 8xMS2.

claim: The MASS system overcomes the obstacle of inserting a 1300 nt 24xMS2 into the genome for imaging endogenous mRNAs.
source: Here, we describe an MS2-based signal amplification with the Suntag system that enables live-cell RNA imaging of high temporal resolution and with 8xMS2 stem-loops, which overcomes the obstacle of inserting a 1300 nt 24xMS2 into the genome for the imaging of endogenous mRNAs.
evidence: The manuscript demonstrates successful imaging of endogenous mRNAs in C. elegans using 8xMS2 knock-ins, which are shorter than 24xMS2.

claim: The MASS system was used to image the activation of gene expression in the epidermis of live C. elegans.
source: Using this tool, we were able to image the activation of gene expression and the dynamics of endogenous mRNAs in the epidermis of live C. elegans.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing wound-induced gene expression activation in C. elegans epidermis (Figure 2).

claim: The MASS system was used to image the dynamics of endogenous mRNAs in the epidermis of live C. elegans.
source: Using this tool, we were able to image the activation of gene expression and the dynamics of endogenous mRNAs in the epidermis of live C. elegans.
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing mRNA dynamics in C. elegans (Figure 2D-G).

claim: Live-cell imaging of RNAs at a single-molecule level is crucial to uncovering their roles in gene expression regulation.
source: Live-cell imaging of RNAs at a single-molecule level is crucial to uncovering their roles in gene expression regulation (Buxbaum et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Various tools have been developed to visualize RNAs in live cells.
source: Various tools have been developed to visualize RNAs in live cells (Braselmann et al., 2020; Le et al., 2022), including RNA-binding protein–fluorescent protein approaches (Bertrand et al., 1998), CRISPR-based systems (Nelles et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2019), and those utilizing fluorophore–RNA aptamer pairs (Chen et al., 2019; Paige et al., 2011; Sunbul et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The MS2-based system is the most widely used and represents the current gold standard for single-molecule RNA imaging in live cells.
source: The MS2-based system is the most widely used and represents the current gold standard for single-molecule RNA imaging in live cells (Braselmann et al., 2020; Bertrand et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: MS2 is a short RNA stem-loop bound specifically by the bacteriophage MS2 coat protein (MCP).
source: MS2 is a short RNA stem-loop bound specifically by the bacteriophage MS2 coat protein (MCP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the MS2 system.

claim: In the MS2 system, 24xMS2 are placed at the 3′UTR or 5′UTR, and a fluorescent protein is fused to the MCP.
source: To image RNA, 24xMS2 are placed at the 3′UTR or 5′UTR, and a fluorescent protein is fused to the MCP (MCP-FP).
evidence: This describes the conventional MS2 system design, which is established knowledge.

claim: When coexpressed in cells, up to 48 fluorescent proteins (2 × 24, with two MCPs bound to one MS2) will be recruited to the RNA through MS2–MCP binding.
source: When coexpressed in cells, up to 48 fluorescent proteins (2 × 24, with two MCPs bound to one MS2) will be recruited to the RNA through MS2–MCP binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known stoichiometry of MS2-MCP binding.

claim: The MS2 system has been successfully used to trace the whole mRNA life-cycle from transcription, to nuclear export, subcellular localization, translation, and to final degradation.
source: The MS2 system has been successfully used to trace the whole mRNA life-cycle from transcription, to nuclear export, subcellular localization, translation, and to final degradation (Braselmann et al., 2020; Le et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Most RNA imaging studies in animal cells have been performed using exogenous mRNAs in cultured cell lines.
source: However, most RNA imaging studies in animal cells have been performed using exogenous mRNAs in cultured cell lines.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, reflecting established knowledge.

claim: 24xMS2 (about 1300 nt in length) have to be knocked into a specific genomic locus to image endogenous mRNA.
source: 24xMS2 (about 1300 nt in length) have to be knocked into a specific genomic locus to image endogenous mRNA.
evidence: This describes the requirement for endogenous mRNA imaging using the conventional MS2 system, which is established knowledge.

claim: The difficulty and low efficiency of the knock-in of long sequences into the genome represent a significant obstacle toward visualizing endogenous mRNA using the MS2 system.
source: The difficulty and low efficiency of the knock-in of long sequences into the genome represent a significant obstacle toward visualizing endogenous mRNA using the MS2 system.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges in the field, reflecting established knowledge.

claim: Less than 10 endogenous mRNAs have been imaged in live animal cells at a single-molecule level.
source: Thus, it is not surprising that less than 10 endogenous mRNAs have been imaged in live animal cells at a single-molecule level, and examples of endogenous mRNAs imaged in live animals remain extremely rare (Halstead et al., 2015; Levo et al., 2022; Dufourt et al., 2021; Park et al., 2014; Das et al., 2018; Zimyanin et al., 2008; Forrest and Gavis, 2003; Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Examples of endogenous mRNAs imaged in live animals remain extremely rare.
source: Thus, it is not surprising that less than 10 endogenous mRNAs have been imaged in live animal cells at a single-molecule level, and examples of endogenous mRNAs imaged in live animals remain extremely rare (Halstead et al., 2015; Levo et al., 2022; Dufourt et al., 2021; Park et al., 2014; Das et al., 2018; Zimyanin et al., 2008; Forrest and Gavis, 2003; Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Overexpressed mRNAs may not faithfully recapitulate endogenous mRNA expression and dynamics.
source: Since overexpressed mRNAs may not faithfully recapitulate endogenous mRNA expression and dynamics, the development of more sensitive techniques for endogenous mRNA imaging is of great value.
evidence: This is a statement reflecting established knowledge about the limitations of overexpression systems.

claim: Combining the MS2 with a signal amplifier may allow the recruitment of more fluorescent proteins to the RNA with fewer MS2 repeats.
source: In this study, we reasoned that combining the MS2 with a signal amplifier may allow the recruitment of more fluorescent proteins to the RNA with fewer MS2 repeats (i.e., 8xMS2 – see Figure 1A).
evidence: This is the reasoning behind the MASS system design, which is then validated by experimental data.

claim: Suntag is a 19 amino acid protein tag that binds to its specific single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody.
source: Suntag is a 19 amino acid protein tag that binds to its specific single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibody (Tanenbaum et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In the MASS system, one MS2 interacts with two MCP-24xSuntag molecules, further recruiting 2 × 24 GFP molecules.
source: When coexpressed in cells, one MS2 interacts with two MCP-24xSuntag molecules, further recruiting 2 × 24 GFP molecules (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the design principle of MASS, which is an inference based on the known stoichiometry of MS2-MCP and Suntag-scFv binding.

claim: When an 8xMS2 is placed into the 3′UTR, up to 384 (2 × 8 × 24) GFP can be tethered to a single mRNA through the MCP–Suntag–scFv–sfGFP interaction.
source: When an 8xMS2 is placed into the 3′UTR, up to 384 (2 × 8 × 24) GFP can then be tethered to a single mRNA through the MCP–Suntag–scFv–sfGFP interaction (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the stoichiometry of the MASS system components.

claim: The MASS system leads to the formation of an intense GFP spot associated with single mRNA, facilitating live RNA imaging.
source: This leads to the formation of an intense GFP spot associated with single mRNA, facilitating live RNA imaging.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing bright GFP foci in cells expressing the MASS system (Figure 1B).

claim: Bright GFP foci were readily detected when all the required elements of the MASS (MS2, MCP, 24xSuntag, and scFv antibody) were present.
source: When all the required elements of the MASS (MS2, MCP, 24xSuntag, and scFv antibody) were present, bright GFP foci were readily detected (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: No GFP foci were detected when omitting any one of the MASS elements (MS2, MCP, 24xSuntag, or scFv antibody).
source: As controls, no GFP foci were detected when omitting any one of these elements (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MCP-24xSuntag particles were not detected under the imaging conditions used (100–500 ms exposure time).
source: Under our imaging conditions (100–500 ms exposure time), MCP-24xSuntag particles were not detected (Figure 1B), probably because MCP-24xSuntag are diffusing too fast to be imaged as a spot.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and an inference about the reason.

claim: The GFP foci detected by MASS represent β-ACTIN RNA molecules.
source: Thus, the GFP foci clearly represent β-ACTIN RNA molecules.
evidence: This is inferred from the control experiments showing no foci when any MASS component is missing.

claim: MASS detected a similar number of GFP foci compared to the spots detected by smFISH.
source: We found that MASS detected a similar number of GFP foci compared to the spots detected by smFISH (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The majority of GFP foci (72%) colocalized with the smFISH spots of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs.
source: Moreover, the majority of GFP foci (72%) colocalized with the smFISH spots of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs (Figure 1C, D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, D.

claim: Not all MS2 stem-loop will be bound by the MCP.
source: It is reported that not all MS2 stem-loop will be bound by the MCP (Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: MASS is able to detect single mRNA molecules and label the majority of mRNAs from a specific gene in live cells.
source: Taken together, our data indicated that MASS is able to detect single mRNA molecules and label the majority of mRNAs from a specific gene in live cells.
evidence: This is supported by the smFISH colocalization data and the detection of similar numbers of foci.

claim: Tagging mRNAs with MS2 stem-loops might affect mRNA stability.
source: It was reported that tagging mRNAs with MS2 stem-loops might affect mRNA stability, which could be counteracted by using improved versions of MS2 repeats (Li et al., 2022; Vera et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs were detected regardless of using MS2-V14 or MS2-V721 with 2× tandem repeats of monomer MCPs (tdMCP).
source: We found GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs were detected regardless of using MS2-V14 or MS2-V721 with 2× tandem repeats of monomer MCPs (tdMCP) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: MASS could be performed using different versions of MS2 stem-loops and MCPs.
source: Therefore, MASS could be performed using different versions of MS2 stem-loops and MCPs.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing successful imaging with different MS2 versions.

claim: The stability of MYC, HSPA1A, and KIF18B mRNAs was not significantly affected by tagging of 8xMS2 V1 or by coexpression of the MASS imaging system.
source: We found that the stability of those mRNAs was not significantly affected either by tagging of 8xMS2 V1 or by coexpression of the MASS imaging system (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, C.

claim: β-ACTIN mRNAs with 3′UTR can localize to the lamellipodia.
source: It has been reported that β-ACTIN mRNAs with 3′UTR can localize to the lamellipodia (Katz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNAs were localized to the lamellipodia in HeLa cells.
source: In support of this, we observed that the GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNAs were indeed localized to the lamellipodia in HeLa cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and Video 1.

claim: GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR mRNAs detected by MASS or 24xMS2 system showed similar localization in NIH/3T3 cells.
source: We found that GFP foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR mRNAs detected by MASS or 24xMS2 system showed similar localization (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: MASS did not affect RNA subcellular localization.
source: Thus, these data suggested that MASS did not affect RNA subcellular localization.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing similar localization patterns with MASS and conventional MS2 system.

claim: The conventional 24xMS2 mRNA imaging system detected β-ACTIN-3′UTR mRNAs with a signal-to-noise ratio of 1.21.
source: This strategy allows the detection of β-ACTIN-3′UTR mRNAs with a signal-to-noise ratio of 1.21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A, B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A, B.

claim: MASS with MCP-24xSuntag showed the highest signal-to-ratio of 1.79.
source: MASS with MCP-24xSuntag showed the highest signal-to-ratio of 1.79.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: MCP-12xSuntag and MCP-6xSuntag labeled β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs with a similar signal-to-noise ratio of 1.42 and 1.48, which are better than the conventional 24xMS2 system.
source: MCP-12xSuntag and MCP-6xSuntag labeled β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8xMS2 mRNAs with a similar signal-to-noise ratio of 1.42 and 1.48, which are better than the conventional 24xMS2 system (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–I, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–I.

claim: MASS is flexible regarding the length of Suntag repeats used for imaging.
source: Thus, MASS is flexible regarding the length of Suntag repeats used for imaging.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing successful imaging with different Suntag lengths.

claim: MASS with short repeats of Suntag (MCP-6xSuntag) is sufficient for RNA labeling.
source: MASS with short repeats of Suntag (MCP-6xSuntag) is sufficient for RNA labeling.
evidence: This is supported by the signal-to-noise data showing effective labeling with MCP-6xSuntag.

claim: mRNA labeled by MASS with MCP-24xSuntag or MCP-12xSuntag showed a smaller velocity compared to the conventional 24xMS2 system.
source: We found that compared to the conventional 24xMS2 system, mRNA labeled by MASS with MCP-24xSuntag or MCP-12xSuntag showed a smaller velocity (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B, Figure 1—source data 1), indicating that heavier labeling affected mRNA movement speed.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B.

claim: Heavier labeling affected mRNA movement speed.
source: We found that compared to the conventional 24xMS2 system, mRNA labeled by MASS with MCP-24xSuntag or MCP-12xSuntag showed a smaller velocity (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B, Figure 1—source data 1), indicating that heavier labeling affected mRNA movement speed.
evidence: This is inferred from the velocity data comparing different labeling intensities.

claim: mRNAs labeled by MASS with MCP-6xSuntag showed a similar velocity to that labeled with the conventional 24xMS2 system.
source: In contrast, mRNAs labeled by MASS with MCP-6xSuntag showed a similar velocity to that labeled with the conventional 24xMS2 system (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B.

claim: When MASS is used to measure the speed of mRNA movement, a short Suntag array (MCP-6xSuntag) should be used.
source: Those data pointed out that when MASS is used to measure the speed of mRNA movement, a short Suntag array (MCP-6xSuntag) should be used.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the velocity data showing that MCP-6xSuntag does not affect mRNA movement speed.

claim: GFP foci detected by MASS showed higher intensity than those detected by the 24xMS2 system.
source: We found GFP foci detected by MASS showed higher intensity than those detected by the 24xMS2 system (Figure 1—figure supplement 6, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: With MASS, a single mRNA molecule could be tethered with more GFP molecules, forming a GFP spot of higher fluorescence intensity.
source: These data support that with MASS, a single mRNA molecule could be tethered with more GFP molecules, forming a GFP spot of higher fluorescence intensity.
evidence: This is inferred from the intensity data showing higher fluorescence with MASS.

claim: MASS retains the ability to image mRNA using low-power lasers, thus lowering any unwanted phototoxicity and photobleaching.
source: Such an application, retains the ability to image mRNA using low-power lasers, thus lowering any unwanted phototoxicity and photobleaching and still allowing the tracking of mRNA dynamics in high temporal resolution.
evidence: This is an inference based on the higher fluorescence intensity of MASS-labeled mRNAs.

claim: MASS allows the tracking of mRNA dynamics in high temporal resolution.
source: Such an application, retains the ability to image mRNA using low-power lasers, thus lowering any unwanted phototoxicity and photobleaching and still allowing the tracking of mRNA dynamics in high temporal resolution.
evidence: This is supported by the time-lapse imaging data showing mRNA dynamics at 1-2 second intervals.

claim: β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNA foci showed fusion dynamics where GFP spots fused into a more prominent spot.
source: We found that foci of mRNAs showed various dynamics: (1) Fusion. GFP spots fused into a more prominent spot (Figure 1E and Video 3);
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Video 3.

claim: β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNA foci showed fission dynamics where large GFP foci split into smaller spots.
source: (2) Fission. Large GFP foci split into smaller spots (Figure 1F and Video 4);
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Video 4.

claim: β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNA foci showed transient interaction dynamics where GFP foci touched each other briefly, then moved away.
source: (3) Transient interaction. GFP foci touched each other briefly, then moved away (Figure 1G and Video 5), suggesting there are dynamic RNA–RNA interactions in cells;
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and Video 5.

claim: There are dynamic RNA–RNA interactions in cells.
source: (3) Transient interaction. GFP foci touched each other briefly, then moved away (Figure 1G and Video 5), suggesting there are dynamic RNA–RNA interactions in cells;
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of transient interactions between mRNA foci.

claim: Some β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNA foci showed little movement, suggesting that these mRNAs may be anchored to subcellular structures.
source: (4) Dynamic movement or anchoring. Despite most foci of β-ACTIN-3′UTR-8XMS2 mRNAs showing dynamic movement in cells, other foci were far more static, showing little movement (Figure 1H and Video 6), suggesting that these latter mRNAs may be anchored to subcellular structures.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H and Video 6, with an inference about anchoring.

claim: The knock-in of short sequences into the genome is far more efficient than those of longer sequences.
source: It has been previously reported that the knock-in of short sequences into the genome is far more efficient than those of longer sequences (Wang et al., 2022; Paix et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The MASS exploits the advantage that only 8xMS2 (350 nt) needs to be inserted into a genomic locus.
source: The MASS exploits this advantage as only 8xMS2 (350 nt) needs to be inserted into a genomic locus, thus overcoming the previous obstacle of the requirement of inserting a long 1300 nt 24xMS2 into the genome for live-cell imaging of endogenous mRNA.
evidence: This is a statement about the design advantage of MASS, which is then validated by successful endogenous mRNA imaging in C. elegans.

claim: Bright GFP foci could only be detected when all the required elements of MASS were present in C. elegans epidermis.
source: Consistent with the observations in HeLa cells, bright GFP foci could only be detected when all the required elements were present (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Excluding any essential elements of MASS resulted in a complete failure of foci formation in C. elegans.
source: Similarly, excluding any essential elements resulted in a complete failure of foci formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The MASS was efficient in imaging exogenous RNAs in live animals.
source: Thus, the MASS was efficient in imaging exogenous RNAs in live animals.
evidence: This is inferred from the successful imaging of cdc-42-8xMS2 in C. elegans.

claim: Upon wounding the C. elegans epithelium via laser or needle, specific gene expressions and downstream signaling cascades for wound repair are triggered and activated.
source: Upon wounding the epithelium via laser or needle, specific gene expressions and downstream signaling cascades for wound repair are then triggered and activated (Xu and Chisholm, 2014; Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The expression levels of C42D4.3 and mai-1 were reported to increase significantly after wounding.
source: To this end, 8xMS2 was knocked into the 3′UTR region of two endogenous genes, C42D4.3 and mai-1 (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), the expression levels of which were reported to increase significantly after wounding (Fu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Prior to wounding, few sfGFP foci were detected in either wild-type or in 8xMS2 knock-in animals.
source: Prior to wounding, few sfGFP foci were detected in either wild-type (WT) or in 8xMS2 knock-in animals (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Numerous GFP foci were formed 15 min after wounding in the C42D4.3 and mai-1 8xMS2 knock-in animals but not in the WT animals.
source: In contrast, numerous GFP foci were formed 15 min after wounding in the C42D4.3 and mai-1 8xMS2 knock-in animals but not in the WT animals (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Videos 7–9).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Wounding activated C42D4.3 and mai-1 mRNA expression.
source: This result suggests that the wounding had activated C42D4.3 and mai-1 mRNA expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the appearance of GFP foci after wounding and confirmed by qRT-PCR data.

claim: C42D4.3 and mai-1 mRNA levels were upregulated more than eightfold 15 min after injury.
source: In agreement with this, qRT-PCR showed that C42D4.3 and mai-1 mRNA levels were upregulated more than eightfold 15 min after injury (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Figure 2—source data 1), confirming that GFP foci were able to detect endogenous C42D4.3–8xMS2 and mai-1-8xMS2 mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: GFP foci were able to detect endogenous C42D4.3–8xMS2 and mai-1-8xMS2 mRNAs.
source: In agreement with this, qRT-PCR showed that C42D4.3 and mai-1 mRNA levels were upregulated more than eightfold 15 min after injury (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Figure 2—source data 1), confirming that GFP foci were able to detect endogenous C42D4.3–8xMS2 and mai-1-8xMS2 mRNAs.
evidence: This is confirmed by the correlation between GFP foci appearance and qRT-PCR data.

claim: The expression level of C42D4.3 mRNA was similar in WT, C42D4.3 8xMS2 knock-in animals and animals expressing the MASS imaging system.
source: In addition, the expression level (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C, Figure 2—source data 1) and stability of C42D4.3 mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, Figure 2—source data 1) were similar in WT, C42D4.3 8xMS2 knock-in animals and animals expressing the MASS imaging system, indicating MASS did not affect the expression level and stability of endogenous C42D4.3 mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The stability of C42D4.3 mRNA was similar in WT, C42D4.3 8xMS2 knock-in animals and animals expressing the MASS imaging system.
source: In addition, the expression level (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C, Figure 2—source data 1) and stability of C42D4.3 mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, Figure 2—source data 1) were similar in WT, C42D4.3 8xMS2 knock-in animals and animals expressing the MASS imaging system, indicating MASS did not affect the expression level and stability of endogenous C42D4.3 mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: MASS did not affect the expression level and stability of endogenous C42D4.3 mRNAs.
source: In addition, the expression level (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C, Figure 2—source data 1) and stability of C42D4.3 mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, Figure 2—source data 1) were similar in WT, C42D4.3 8xMS2 knock-in animals and animals expressing the MASS imaging system, indicating MASS did not affect the expression level and stability of endogenous C42D4.3 mRNAs.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing similar expression and stability across conditions.

claim: GFP foci were detected as early as 1 min after wounding in proximity to the injury site.
source: We found that in proximity to the injury site GFP foci were detected as early as 1 min after wounding (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: No GFP foci could be detected after wounding when C. elegans were pretreated with Actinomycin D.
source: As a control, we pretreated the C. elegans with Actinomycin D, which potently inhibits gene transcription. In such cases, no GFP foci could be detected after wounding (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: GFP foci are newly synthesized C42D4.3–8xMS2 mRNAs.
source: This indicated that GFP foci are newly synthesized C42D4.3–8xMS2 mRNAs.
evidence: This is inferred from the Actinomycin D control experiment showing no foci when transcription is inhibited.

claim: Gene expression activation and transcription occur extremely fast (within 1 min after the stimulation).
source: Our data demonstrated that gene expression activation and transcription occur extremely fast (in this case, within 1 min after the stimulation).
evidence: This is supported by the observation of GFP foci appearing 1 min after wounding.

claim: The appearance of GFP foci gradually spreads from the area around the injury site to distal regions.
source: In addition, the appearance of GFP foci gradually spreads from the area around the injury site to distal regions.
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The total foci number steadily increased in the epidermis after wounding.
source: The total foci number steadily increased in the epidermis (Figure 2D, E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D, E.

claim: Wounding generated a signal to activate downstream gene expression around the injury site.
source: These data suggested that wounding generated a signal to activate downstream gene expression around the injury site.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial and temporal pattern of GFP foci appearance after wounding.

claim: The wound signal was diffused to distal regions and able to induce gene expression there.
source: The signal was then diffused to distal regions and able to induce gene expression there.
evidence: This is inferred from the spreading pattern of GFP foci from the wound site to distal regions.

claim: GFP foci preferentially underwent fusion leading to increased foci size.
source: In addition, GFP foci preferentially underwent fusion leading to increased foci size (Figure 2F, G, and Video 10, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F, G.

claim: Fusion events of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs were not frequently observed in the epidermis.
source: In contrast, when exogenous BFP-8xMS2 was expressed and imaged with MASS in the epidermis (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A, Figure 2—source data 1), such fusion events were not frequently observed (Video 11), and the puncta size of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs kept constant in 5 min (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A–C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and Video 11.

claim: The puncta size of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs kept constant in 5 min.
source: In contrast, when exogenous BFP-8xMS2 was expressed and imaged with MASS in the epidermis (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A, Figure 2—source data 1), such fusion events were not frequently observed (Video 11), and the puncta size of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs kept constant in 5 min (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A–C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A–C.

claim: The puncta size of C42D4.3-8xMS2 mRNAs was significantly larger than that of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs.
source: In addition, the puncta size of C42D4.3-8xMS2 mRNAs was significantly larger than that of BFP-8xMS2 mRNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5C.

claim: C42D4.3 mRNAs undergo clustering after wounding and form RNA granules in vivo.
source: These data suggested that C42D4.3 mRNAs undergo clustering after wounding and form RNA granules in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the fusion events and increased foci size of C42D4.3 mRNAs after wounding.

claim: mRNAs formed large clusters and are co-translated in Drosophila embryos.
source: In agreement with our observation, it has been previously reported that mRNAs formed large clusters and are co-translated in Drosophila embryos (Dufourt et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The SunRISER and MoonRISER system by combination of PP7 and Suntag or Moontag enables imaging of single exogenous mRNAs in living cells.
source: It has been recently reported that the SunRISER and MoonRISER system by combination of PP7 and Suntag or Moontag enables imaging of single exogenous mRNAs in living cells.
evidence: This is a statement about prior work in the field.

claim: SunRISER provided an excellent approach for long-term imaging of overexpressed mRNA in living cells.
source: Through computational and experimental approaches, the authors further optimized the SunRISER system and showed that SunRISER provided an excellent approach for long-term imaging of overexpressed mRNA in living cells (Guo and Lee, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The principle of the SunRISER system and MASS is similar, which uses a protein signal amplifier to generate a higher fluorescence signal for RNA imaging.
source: The principle of the SunRISER system and MASS is similar, which uses a protein signal amplifier to generate a higher fluorescence signal for RNA imaging.
evidence: This is a comparison between MASS and a related system, based on their design principles.

claim: MASS is valuable for imaging endogenous mRNAs that utilizing only 8xMS2 in comparison to the 24xMS2 used in the classic MS2-based live-cell RNA imaging.
source: Here, we showed such signal amplification strategy is valuable for imaging endogenous mRNAs that utilizing only 8xMS2 in comparison to the 24xMS2 used in the classic MS2-based live-cell RNA imaging.
evidence: This is supported by the successful imaging of endogenous mRNAs in C. elegans using 8xMS2.

claim: The advantage of a short MS2 is of prime benefits for imaging endogenous mRNA as it reduced difficulties involved in inserting a long 1300 nt 24xMS2 into a genomic locus.
source: The advantage of a short MS2 is of prime benefits for imaging endogenous mRNA as it reduced difficulties involved in inserting a long 1300 nt 24xMS2 into a genomic locus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known difficulty of long sequence knock-ins and the successful use of 8xMS2 in this study.

claim: MASS will help promote studies of RNA transcription, nuclear export, subcellular localization, translation, RNA sensing, and degradation, at the endogenous level in culture cells and live animals.
source: We expect this tool will help promote studies of RNA transcription, nuclear export, subcellular localization, translation, RNA sensing, and degradation, at the endogenous level in culture cells and live animals.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of MASS.
